newsitem.title: USA: New 144a issues to hit US corporate bond mart.
newsitem.headline: New 144a issues to hit US corporate bond mart.

text.p: Corporate high-grade debt issuance has been put on the backburner for now as a load of high-yield 144A private placement debt offerings take centerstage, dealers said.
"It's very quiet right now with no official calendar out there," said one high-grade syndicate source. It's a continuation of last week's wait-and-see mood in the market."
Despite the lack of an official calendar, syndicate sources cited rumors that Ford Motor Co will bring a $1.0 billion global 10-year debt offering via Merrill Lynch.
The lack of high-grade deals for this week is not expected to spill over into the high-yield arena as a long list of issuers get set to come to market, dealers said.
TCI Satellite Entertainment is expected to issue its $350 million in two-part debt one day this week via joint lead managers Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities and Merrill Lynch.
The deal consist of $150 senior subordinated notes due 2006 and $200 million (proceeds) in senior subordinated discount notes due 2006.
Another $200 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2009 will be brought by to market by KinderCare Learning Centers.
The issue is expected to be callable after five years and price talk is seen between 9.625 - 9.875 percent. Chase Securities is expected to underwrite the deal.
Also, Forcenergy is expected to issue $175 million in 144A B1/B rated senior subordinated notes due 2007, callable after five years, sources said.
Dawson Production Services is also set to bring $110 million in senior notes due 2007, sources said.
Another rumored deal is a two-part offering of 10-year senior notes and 10-year senior discount note by Nextwave Telecommunications, sources added.
Sun Media Corp may also issue $150 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2007 later this week, sources said.

Barret Resoures Corp is expected to tap the market with $150 million in senior notes due 2007. The issue has a make-whole-call and is rated Ba1/BB-plus. Goldman Sachs & Co is expected to underwrite the offering, sources said.

Activity is expected to slow down as players approach the end of the week as U.S. debt markets will see a shortened trading session on Friday as the market heads into Monday's President's Day holiday.
In the government market, the U.S. 30-year bond is up 1/32 at 97-15/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
